key_insight: Replace fixed max-iteration cutoffs with semantic early-stopping so iterative LLM agent loops stop when meaning and quality stop improving, not just when a token budget is exhausted.
engineering_relevance: This can cut unnecessary inference cost in writer-critic or multi-agent workflows while preserving answer quality, making iterative LLM systems more efficient to deploy.
method: Use embedding cosine distance between consecutive drafts with a patience window to detect semantic convergence.
Optionally gate stopping on measured quality improvement using an LLM judge.
Replay the same draft trajectory under multiple stopping policies and cache judge calls for fair, low-cost comparison.
evidence_signal: On 60 HotpotQA test questions, the judge-free semantic stopper reduced operational tokens by 38% versus max_iterations with parity quality (Delta-IS = -0.004, p = 0.81), while the oracle best-round selector beat all practical policies by +0.115 Information Score.
watch_item: Quality-gated stopping may be too expensive in practice because repeated judge calls can outweigh the savings from fewer generation rounds.
paper_title: Semantic Early-Stopping for Iterative LLM Agent Loops
